messages:
Anya: heads-up — trying to onboard a HF model that vendors custom classes (auto_map) and it's tripping our conversion. model repo asks for `trust_remote_code=True` and a custom `ChatTemplate` in config.json. when converted to Redwood format the chat template placeholders are mangled and special tokens disappear.

Stefan: ugh. which model? any stacktrace?

Anya: repo: github.com/username/wasabi-chat-2.0 (private). error during runtime: `KeyError: '<|system|>'` when generating, and token lengths differ between HF tokenizer and our saved tokenizer. snippet from convert log: 
```
Loaded config with AutoConfig -> <class 'vendor.wasabi.WasabiConfig'>
AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)
Saved tokenizer vocab size: 50256
Redwood tokenizer expected size: 50261
```

Mike: sounds like vendor added 5 special tokens in `tokenizer_config.json` and our converter ignored them. are we reading `tokenizer_config.json` or only `tokenizer.json`/merges?

Anya: converter reads `tokenizer.json` + `special_tokens_map` but this model stores specials only in `config.json` under `chat_special_tokens` and also defines a `post_process_template` field. converter didn't parse that custom key.

Nora: can you repro locally and paste the minimal repro? maybe `trust_remote_code` is also bringing in a custom Tokenizer class that mutates tokens on init.

Anya: repro attached in gist: https://gist.github.com/anon/xx (short). quick fix I tried: 
```
# quick workaround
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path, trust_remote_code=True)
added = {'additional_special_tokens': ['<|system|>','<|assistant|>','<|user|>','<|end|>','<|sep|>']}
if set(added['additional_special_tokens']) - set(tok.all_special_tokens):
    tok.add_special_tokens(added)
    tok.save_pretrained(path+'_patched')
```
This fixes KeyError but fails quant tests: q4_k_m quantized runtime gives lower Rouge and weird tokenization boundaries.

Stefan: interesting — vendor tokenizer may be doing byte-level normalization or different pre-tokenization. Adding tokens manually can hide the underlying normalization mismatch. Do you have a diff of tokenizer config before/after?

Anya: yes — prepatched `normalizer`: null, `pre_tokenizer`: {"type":"BPEPresplit"} (custom). After using HF's generic AutoTokenizer init with trust_remote_code it registers vendor class which sets `pre_tokenizer` differently. our converter when not using trust_remote_code was silently falling back to `BPE` and losing those steps.

Mike: that explains quant regression — if token boundaries change, logits map to different token ids causing quality drift after quantization. Also q4_k_m sometimes amplifies small shifts.

Nora: we should update converter to: 1) respect `trust_remote_code` when vendor code is safe (allowlist patterns), 2) vendor-tokenizer bake-in: serialize the tokenizer's `normalizer`/`pre_tokenizer`/`post_processor` into the Redwood tokenizer format, and 3) preserve chat template fields (e.g., `post_process_template`) into our `chat_template` metadata.

Anya: agreed. I prototyped a patch that runs `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)` inside isolated env and dumps `tokenizer.init_args`, `tokenizer.normalizer.__dict__` etc. but worried about executing unknown code at scale.

Stefan: security team note: we can gate `trust_remote_code` behind repo allowlist / checksum verification + run inside a sandboxed build image. not ideal but doable for enterprise onboarding.

ci-bot: build 5821 started for branch wasabi-token-workaround
ci-bot: tests: tokenizer-compat, quant-eval, chat-template-parse

Anya: CI result: tokenizer-compat passed locally but quant-eval failed: delta Rouge-L -0.045 vs baseline, BERTScore -0.03. failure concentrated on prompts with multi-turn system messages.

Mike: can you run a controlled A/B: compare outputs (tokenized sequences) for 100 eval prompts using vendor tokenizer (trust_remote_code) vs our patched tokenizer? If token ids differ at any prefix that's the smoking gun.

Anya: running now. quick sample:
```
prompt: "System: You are assistant...\nUser: What is X?"
vendor tok ids: [1,234,45,67,999, ...]
patched tok ids: [1,234,45,68,997, ...]
```
Mismatch starts at token 4 for many prompts.

Nora: ok then two paths: 1) fully vendor-bake tokenizer into conversion (preferred for fidelity), or 2) normalize vendor pre-tokenization into a deterministic mapping we can reproduce in runtime (hard). For quant/production I'd pick 1.

Mike: vendor-bake means we need to store the vendor tokenizer python code or its serialized normalization steps. For privacy/regulatory customers that won't accept trust_remote_code. fallback?

Anya: fallback plan: if vendor code is blocked, run an offline conversion step in a trusted environment where we allow `trust_remote_code` for build, then export a pure tokenizer artefact (tokenizer.json + normalizer/patterns) and store as a vetted asset. runtime Redwood serving uses the vetted asset, no code execution.

Stefan: sounds good. also add an eval step post-quant to detect tokenization drift: compare tokenization of a fixed prompt set pre/post quant and fail the rollout if > X% mismatch.

Nora: and log a `tokenization_hash` for the model bundle so we can detect accidental changes across conversions.

Anya: I'll open a PR with: converter patch + build sandbox + quant post-check + a small eval harness. cc @Mike @Stefan for review.

Mike: awesome. can you also add a small note in onboarding doc: "models that vendor custom tokenizers require vetted conversion; don't rely on `trust_remote_code` at runtime" :thumbsup:

Anya: yep. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4321 (draft). I'll attach sample logs and the rouge diffs.

Stefan: thanks. one more thing — try q4_k_m vs q4_0/q8_0 in the eval harness to see which quant scheme is less sensitive to token boundary shifts. might prefer q8 for initial canary.

Anya: good call. I'll include that matrix in PR.

Nora: great thread. small followup: when you add `chat_template` metadata, include a mapping table for placeholders we support so template rendering is deterministic across runtimes.

Anya: will do. closing the thread once PR lands. :rocket:
